glance_notes.text: For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the voter-registration deadline is October 4, the absentee-by-mail application deadline is October 24, and early and absentee in-person voting begins 15 days before Election Day.
glance_notes.source_name: Alaska Division of Elections — Election Calendar

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: To register to vote in Alaska, you must be a U.S. citizen, an Alaska resident, and at least 18 years old or turn 18 by Election Day. You cannot be disqualified by a felony involving moral turpitude unless your voting rights have been restored, and you cannot remain registered to vote in another state. Alaska offers online registration for applicants with a current Alaska driver's license or state ID, as well as in-person and paper registration. Paper applications may be submitted through a Regional Elections Office, and the Division lists additional voter-registration agencies around the state.
register.source_name: Alaska Division of Elections — Voter Information
register.internal_note: Supplemental official registration form: https://www.elections.alaska.gov/doc/forms/C03.pdf. The Division states applicants may register up to 90 days before their 18th birthday, but must be 18 by Election Day to vote.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use Alaska's official My Voter Information service to check your voter-registration information. The Division of Elections also uses this service for voters to check absentee application and ballot status. Review your information before an election and update your registration if your name, residence address, or other registration information has changed.
check_registration.source_name: Alaska Division of Elections — My Voter Information
check_registration.internal_note: The Division's voter-information and absentee pages both direct voters to My Voter Information for registration and absentee status checks.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: For most Alaska elections, you must register or update your voter registration at least 30 days before Election Day. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the official election calendar lists October 4, 2026 as the registration and registration-update deadline. Alaska has a limited same-day registration rule for voting for President and Vice President in presidential elections; that exception does not make same-day registration generally available for all contests.
deadlines.glance_value: October 4, 2026 for the November 3 General Election
deadlines.source_name: Alaska Division of Elections — Election Calendar
deadlines.internal_note: Supplemental sources: https://www.elections.alaska.gov/voter-information/ and https://www.elections.alaska.gov/election-information/. The latter identifies the limited presidential same-day registration rule under AS 15.05.014.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use the Alaska Division of Elections polling-place search or Precinct Locator to find your Election Day voting location. The polling-place page can be searched by city or House district, and the Precinct Locator can locate the nearest polling place from an address. Because locations can change, check the official lookup close to Election Day.
polling_place.source_name: Alaska Division of Elections — Polling Place Locations
polling_place.internal_note: The official polling-place page was updated August 16, 2026 and explicitly states that information is subject to change.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Alaska polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. on Election Day. Voters are asked to provide identification at the polling place. If your name is not on the precinct register, your registration information needs to be updated, or you do not have identification, you may be directed to vote a questioned ballot. Questioned ballots are reviewed after Election Day to determine whether the voter was qualified, and eligible ballots are counted.
election_day.source_name: Alaska Division of Elections — Questioned Ballots
election_day.internal_note: Supplemental source for polling hours: https://www.elections.alaska.gov/election-polls/. The questioned-ballot explainer was published August 24, 2026 and directly addresses no-ID, registration-update and not-on-register situations.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Alaska polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. on Election Day. The Division's 2026 calendar specifically lists those hours for the November 3 General Election.
polling_hours.source_name: Alaska Division of Elections — Polling Place Locations
polling_hours.internal_note: Supplemental source: https://www.elections.alaska.gov/calendar/ lists the November 3, 2026 General Election polls as open 7 a.m.–8 p.m. and cites AS 15.15.020.

early_voting.label: Early Voting
early_voting.content: Alaska offers early voting to any voter; no excuse is required. Early voting and absentee in-person voting begin 15 days before Election Day. At a location designated for Early Voting, election workers use a secure connection to verify the voter's registration and residence information when the voter checks in. If the residence information is not current, the voter is required to use the absentee in-person process instead. Locations and hours vary, so use the Division's official Early & Absentee In-Person Voting Locations page for the current election.
early_voting.glance_value: Available to any voter; begins 15 days before Election Day
early_voting.source_name: Alaska Division of Elections — Absentee and Early Voting
early_voting.internal_note: Supplemental current location page: https://www.elections.alaska.gov/avo/. That page explains the operational distinction between designated Early Voting sites and absentee in-person sites.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee & Mail Voting
absentee_mail.content: Alaska is a no-excuse absentee-voting state, so any voter may apply to vote absentee by mail. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the by-mail application deadline is October 24. Mailed voted ballots must be postmarked on or before November 3; a ballot returned in person to a voting location must be delivered by 8:00 p.m. on Election Day. Alaska also offers absentee ballot delivery by online delivery and fax, with separate application and return rules. For the 2026 General Election, applications for those electronic-delivery options are due by 5:00 p.m. Alaska time on November 2.
absentee_mail.glance_value: No excuse required; by-mail application deadline Oct. 24 for Nov. 3, 2026
absentee_mail.source_name: Alaska Division of Elections — Absentee and Early Voting
absentee_mail.internal_note: The official 2026 calendar also confirms November 3 as the postmark deadline for mailed absentee ballots and November 2 at 5 p.m. Alaska Time as the electronic-transmission application deadline.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Alaska requires voters to provide identification when voting at a polling place. The Division's current questioned-ballot guidance states that a voter who does not have identification may still vote using a questioned ballot, which is reviewed after Election Day to determine eligibility. Alaska's voter ID card is one accepted form of identification. Because the current official sources reviewed for this record did not present one consolidated, current reader-facing list of every acceptable Election Day identification document, voters should use the Division of Elections' current instructions or contact the Division if they are unsure whether a particular document will be accepted.
voter_id.glance_value: Identification required; questioned ballot available if a voter has no ID
voter_id.source_name: Alaska Division of Elections — Questioned Ballots
voter_id.flagged_reason: Current official sources directly establish the identification requirement and questioned-ballot fallback, but a single current voter-facing official page listing all acceptable Election Day ID types was not located during this pass.
voter_id.internal_note: Official 2022 Division notice at https://www.elections.alaska.gov/all-registered-voters-are-getting-new-voter-id-cards/ confirms that voters are required to provide identification and that the Alaska voter ID card is accepted. Current 2026 poll-worker materials also address no-ID questioned ballots. Independent checker should locate and verify the controlling current accepted-ID list before upgrading this section.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: The Alaska Division of Elections provides accessibility assistance at polling places and surveys polling sites for ADA accessibility. Voting Tablets provide magnified text, high contrast and audio ballots so voters with disabilities or reading difficulties can vote more independently. In elections with a federal race, Voting Tablets are available at early-voting locations beginning 15 days before the election and at each polling place on Election Day. Alaska also offers special-needs voting for a voter who cannot go to the polls because of age, serious illness or disability; an eligible voter may use a personal representative to pick up and return the ballot under the state's rules.
accessible_voting.source_name: Alaska Division of Elections — Voter Assistance and Accessibility Information
accessible_voting.internal_note: Supplemental official alternative-voting page: https://www.elections.alaska.gov/Core/alternativevotingoptions.php supports special-needs voting and personal-representative restrictions.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Alaska provides special registration and absentee-voting information for active Uniformed Services members, Merchant Marines, commissioned corps members, eligible spouses and dependents, and U.S. citizens living overseas. Military and overseas voters may request ballot delivery by mail or electronic transmission, and ballots for these voters begin going out 45 days before primary and general elections. Alaska allows eligible voters temporarily outside the state to maintain their Alaska residence address when they intend to return; active Uniformed Services members, Merchant Marines, commissioned corps members and spouses are exempt from the intent-to-return requirement described by the Division. U.S. citizens living permanently overseas who were last domiciled in Alaska and meet the state's conditions may register as federal voters for federal elections.
military_overseas.source_name: Alaska Division of Elections — Military, Overseas, and College Voters
military_overseas.internal_note: Supplemental official permanent-overseas page: https://www.elections.alaska.gov/Core/overseaspermanentvoters.php. It describes federal-voter eligibility and application deadlines for U.S. citizens permanently overseas.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: An Alaska resident attending college either inside or outside Alaska may remain registered in Alaska. For voting purposes, the Division says an Alaska resident is someone who resides in the state and intends to remain, or who leaves temporarily with the intent to return. A student outside Alaska may use the last Alaska residence address where the student lived before leaving when registering, updating registration, or applying for an absentee ballot. An out-of-state resident attending college in Alaska who wants to remain a resident of the home state should use that state's voting procedures instead.
student_voting.source_name: Alaska Division of Elections — Military, Overseas, and College Voters
student_voting.internal_note: The Division also maintains a dedicated College Voters page at https://www.elections.alaska.gov/Core/collegevoters.php with the same residence and voting-option guidance.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: The Alaska Division of Elections publishes official sample ballots on its Sample Ballots page, generally about 50 days before an election. The page currently provides the 2026 Primary Election sample ballots. As of August 30, 2026, the November 3 General Election sample ballots were not yet listed on the current-year sample-ballot table. Check the official page again as the General Election approaches.
sample_ballot.source_name: Alaska Division of Elections — Sample Ballots
sample_ballot.flagged_reason: 2026 General Election sample ballots were not yet listed on the official sample-ballot page when checked.
sample_ballot.internal_note: The official page says sample ballots are posted approximately 50 days before an election. Recheck in September 2026.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: The Alaska Division of Elections website is the state's central source for voter registration, My Voter Information, absentee and early voting, polling-place locations, sample ballots, election calendars, accessibility information, military and overseas voting, college-voter information, ballot measures and election results. Use the Division's official tools rather than third-party voter sites when checking your registration, polling place, absentee status or current election materials.
official_resources.internal_note: Primary direct-action resources include My Voter Information at https://myvoterinformation.alaska.gov/, polling places at https://www.elections.alaska.gov/election-polls/, absentee/early voting at https://www.elections.alaska.gov/voter-information/absentee-and-early-voting/, and sample ballots at https://www.elections.alaska.gov/sample-ballots/.
